title: fix: show update canary and Doctor phase timings
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unexplained gaps in `openclaw update` reports when candidate rehearsal, post-stop checks, or runtime activation takes a long time.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish private-state copying, Doctor work, test Gateway startup, cleanup, and activation work instead of treating the entire quiet interval as a slow copy. Doctor diagnostics include section durations and the five slowest contributions.

The installed updater remains the driver: most new timings first appear on the update after installing this change. Pre/post-plugin Doctor timings can appear on the installing hop. Older Doctor candidates without section traces still work without section diagnostics.

## Why This Change Was Made

Git updates discarded successful candidate step results, successful temporary-copy cleanup had no step, and bounded run-history compaction could evict the timing receipts. Keep those receipts, expose the previously untimed activation phases, and reuse Doctor's existing startup-trace phases without introducing a tracing option or changing the run-record shape.

Copy-scope investigation: the canary already snapshots registered SQLite databases and copies exec approvals/configured plugin trees, not `worktrees/`, `workspace/`, or `tmp/`. Synthetic file counts do not change that copy. Peanutto's approximately 40-minute silent stretch is therefore not explained by copying those directories; these timings will identify the slow phase on the next real update. No copy-scope reduction is implemented.

## Evidence

- Retained synthetic-state experiment: adding 0, 25,000, 100,000, and 250,000 unrelated state files left the copied database byte count fixed at 1,757,184. Snapshot-only runs copied three files (1,692 KiB) in 1.2–3.0 seconds. Full-canary reruns varied with host contention rather than unrelated file count; Doctor and Gateway startup dominated.
- Core typecheck and focused lint passed. After the history/receipt repairs, 174 focused tests passed; the final six-case fresh-Doctor timing table also passed, including nonzero and timeout advisories. Earlier focused canary, activation, and finalization coverage remains applicable.
- The existing `persists streamed candidate progress through its admitted worker (reopened)` test hit its unchanged 120-second timeout both here and on the exact clean merge base (`7008414e344`), including a single-worker isolated run. No timeout or assertion was weakened.
- Backward compatibility: a literal pre-timing row fixture, validated against the published 2026.9.8 and main schemas, still loads, lists, and compacts with unchanged identity/timestamps/core facts. A 32-key × approximately 1 KiB Doctor refusal now compacts while preserving timing and bounded refusal context.
- Native published-driver compatibility: installed 2026.9.8 (`fc23bc864e4`) updated successfully to `14833345b1e9`; source HEAD and built commit match, the Gateway returned readiness HTTP 200, and the run finished `succeeded`. The candidate-side post-plugin Doctor recorded 87.078 s with section diagnostics (78.2 s across sections). Canary/activation timing remains absent on this installing hop because the published driver owns those phases.

Single-run native attribution (`14833345b1e9` → identical tree plus an empty commit `6c40e71a42bd`; not a speed comparison) also finished successfully with matching source/build commits and readiness HTTP 200:

| Recorded step | Duration |
| --- | ---: |
| Canary state copy | 25.441 s |
| Canary Doctor | 61.175 s |
| Canary Gateway startup | 23.088 s |
| Canary cleanup | 2.097 s |
| Other canary checks | 40.567 s |
| Post-stop checks (two passes) | 4.901 s + 4.299 s |
| Git checkout | 1.932 s |
| Runtime activation | 0.113 s |
| Activation Doctor | 23.454 s |
| Post-plugin Doctor | 22.987 s |

Doctor section sums were 46.5/61.175 s for the canary, 21.3/23.454 s for activation, and 21.9/22.987 s post-plugin; process/bootstrap overhead is outside those section spans. The full canary steps sum to 152.368 s. **Accounting limit:** all reported step durations total 811.368 s, versus 1,875.067 s for the overall run; the validating phase alone is 1,632.268 s. These receipts expose the requested phases, but do not yet account for the full phase totals. No claim of complete wall-time attribution is made.

The candidate Gateway also successfully listed the published driver's existing run through `update.runs.list`, preserving its successful outcome and history.
- Negative control: the new timing assertions were transplanted onto production code at merge base `7008414e344`. All 17 selected cases failed for absent timing/trace/retention behavior, not test setup; they pass with the change. Commands used `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> -t <selector>`:

  | Suite | Selector | Expected pre-fix failures |
  | --- | --- | ---: |
  | `update-command-execution-validation.test.ts` | `reports Git candidate\|reports the post-stop` | 2 |
  | `update-command-fresh-doctor.test.ts` | `records the fresh Doctor` | 6 |
  | `update-command-package-doctor.test.ts` | `records the activation Doctor` | 1 |
  | `update-finalization-lifecycle.test.ts` | `preserves .* duration and section` | 2 |
  | `update-candidate-canary.test.ts` | `rehearses private state\|records the rehearsal Doctor` | 2 |
  | `update-runner-git-candidate.test.ts` | `reports candidate checks` | 1 |
  | `update-run-ledger.compaction.test.ts` | entire suite before the compatibility case was added | 3 |

Paired synthetic copy study (two alternating runs per state; median and min–max, not a speedup claim):

| Unrelated files | Copied SQLite bytes | Copy median (range) | Whole-canary median (range) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 1,757,184 | 6.36 s (1.72–11.01) | 101.81 s (58.69–144.92) |
| 250,000 | 1,757,184 | 3.08 s (2.45–3.71) | 90.35 s (80.26–100.44) |

The large overlapping spread reflects host contention; unrelated file count does not expand the copied state. This is attribution work, not an update-speed improvement.

The untouched `model-catalog-decisions.ts` line-count warning has the same file blob on the merge base and this branch (`7c1b6e01f07a155aac10409b18c5822277b96ede`). The changed update modules were split at their Doctor-completion and result-settlement seams and pass focused lint.

Merge danger: two-way door. This changes timing/reporting only, not update decisions, configuration, schemas, or persisted record shape. Run-history changes only eviction priority within the existing bounds. A revert removes the additional observations. The blast radius is update diagnostics and their bounded history.
